channel.title: Piotr Zawieja — Writing
channel.description: Analytics engineering, dbt, Snowflake, and AI-assisted data systems.

item.title: Reconciling competing metric definitions across teams with an LLM
item.description: An LLM can't decide what 'active customer' means. It can find every definition you have, show where they diverge, and draft the doc.

item.title: Forecasting with an LLM vs. a real time-series model: where each one is the right call
item.description: An LLM is good at explaining a forecast, not producing one. Where Prophet or ETS still beats asking Claude to predict next quarter's numbers.

item.title: Snowflake clustering keys: what they are, when they help, and when to skip them
item.description: Clustering keys improve query performance by rearranging micro-partitions — but they cost credits continuously. Here is when the trade-off is worth it.

item.title: Idempotency in dbt: the one pipeline property worth obsessing over
item.description: Most dbt models look idempotent but aren't. What breaks it silently and the concrete patterns — unique_key, surrogate keys, partition replacement — that fix it.

item.title: AI for analytics engineering: where it actually helps and where it doesn't
item.description: Not a hype piece. Where AI tools earn their place in an analytics engineering workflow — and where they consistently fall short.

item.title: dbt packages worth using in 2026
item.description: An honest assessment of which dbt packages actually earn their dependency weight — and which ones add complexity without proportional value.

item.title: Dimensional modeling in dbt: the patterns that don't fit the textbook
item.description: Kimball tells you what to build, dbt gives you the tools. Where SCD Type 2 snapshots, bridge tables, and role-playing dimensions actually live.

item.title: How to write dbt tests that catch real business logic errors (not just nulls)
item.description: Most dbt test suites catch infrastructure failures like nulls and duplicate keys, but miss the business logic errors that surface in weekly business reviews.

item.title: dbt Semantic Layer vs. homegrown metric marts: when to use which
item.description: A practical decision framework for analytics engineers choosing between pre-aggregated metric marts and the dbt Semantic Layer with MetricFlow.

item.title: Snowflake Cortex Analyst in practice: what the demo doesn't show you
item.description: Cortex Analyst looks smooth in a demo. Here is what actually happens when you point it at a real warehouse in week two.

item.title: AI-assisted SQL review: using Claude to catch data quality issues before they ship
item.description: Not 'AI is transforming data teams' — a concrete workflow: the prompt, what it catches reliably, and where it fails. For analytics engineers who review dbt PRs.

item.title: Late-arriving data: the silent failure that breaks your incremental models
item.description: Your dbt run succeeds. Tests pass. The dashboard looks fine. The data is still wrong. Late-arriving events and the dbt patterns that handle them correctly.

item.title: dbt incremental models: the complete guide
item.description: How incremental models work, when each strategy applies, and the patterns that only surface after something breaks in production.

item.title: How I set up Claude Code for analytics engineering work
item.description: Most analytics engineers re-explain their stack every AI session. CLAUDE.md, skills, and a few conventions make Claude useful from the first prompt.

item.title: Why governed AI on your warehouse beats RAG on your docs
item.description: Most enterprise data AI projects start by indexing documentation — here is why that is backwards, and what a warehouse-native approach looks like instead.

item.title: How to build a modern analytics data platform: the decisions nobody documents
item.description: Everyone writes about the tools. Nobody writes about the architectural choices made in the first three months that you cannot change without rebuilding.

item.title: From Excel to dbt: a realistic transition guide for Polish data teams
item.description: A practitioner's guide to migrating analytics from spreadsheets to dbt, covering the governance and trust-building steps that most teams skip.

item.title: Why your dbt project has 47 models and nobody trusts any of them
item.description: The dbt trust problem isn't a tooling issue — it's architectural. It shows up in every team that moved fast and skipped the governance layer.
